This allows the temperature to drift beyond the original set point during the on-peak window, trading decreased thermal comfort for reduced peak load. How quickly the temperature drifts to the modified set point will depend on the building’s characteristics, such as the thermal mass, the amount of insulation, and the infiltration. 1.2.3 Set Point Change and Magnitude Different durations of pre-peak load shifting and different set point offsets for load shifting or load shedding can be applied by HVAC load flexibility programs. For a mild impact on residents, a shorter on-peak duration (e.g., 2 hours) with a small set point offset during the on- peak hour (e.g., 2°F) can be used. In contrast, for the maximum load change, a longer pre-peak period (e.g., 4 hours) with larger set point adjustments, such as a low precooling set point (e.g., 60°F) and/or a high on-peak cooling set point (e.g., 80°F), may be applied. 3 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Typically, on-peak periods last 1–4 hours, and the set point is adjusted by 1–4°F during peak periods to align with residents’ comfort preferences. Load- shifting preheating or precooling strategies are not widely adopted in the current programs surveyed for this analysis.
